keyVerseText: Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.
rootMeaning: The name עַמִּיאֵל (ʻAmmîyʼêl) is derived from two Hebrew elements: עַם (ʻam), meaning 'people' or 'kinsman,' and אֵל (El), meaning 'God.' Together, they form a compound meaning 'my kinsman is God' or 'people of God.' This root sense highlights a personal and communal relationship with God, emphasizing both kinship and divine connection beyond a mere tribal or national identity.
usageInScripture: The name Ammiel appears six times in Scripture, consistently as a proper masculine name. It refers to several individuals, including a spy from the tribe of Dan, a father of notable descendants, and a temple doorkeeper. The translations vary slightly between 'Ammiel' and 'of Ammiel,' reflecting both the personal name and patronymic usage. This range shows the name's rootedness in Israelite history and its association with different roles and tribes.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עַמִּיאֵל as 'my kinsman is God' enriches our grasp of biblical identity, where God is not distant but intimately related to His people as a kinsman. This reflects the covenantal relationship God establishes with Israel and ultimately points forward to Christ, the ultimate kinsman-redeemer who identifies with humanity. The name reminds believers that God is not only sovereign but also personally connected to His people, providing security and belonging within His family.
keyVerseReflection: In Numbers 13:12, the text states, 'Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli,' identifying Ammiel as a member of the Danite community. The name's meaning, 'my kinsman is God,' adds depth to this identification, suggesting that even in his role as a spy, Ammiel's identity is rooted in God's kinship. This highlights the theological truth that every member of God's people carries a divine relationship that shapes their role and purpose within the community.
